title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 103: Quorum for meetings

content.overview: Section 103 sets statutory minimum quorum for general meetings, subject to the articles providing a larger number, and prescribes what happens when quorum is absent at the appointed time and at an adjourned meeting.
content.glance: Check the company type, member count, articles and personal presence. Section 103 sets different public-company thresholds and a two-member threshold for private companies, with adjournment/cancellation rules. This section does not apply to an OPC: see section 122(1) and its separate procedure.
content.study:
## Minimum quorum
Unless the articles provide for a larger number, a public company’s quorum is five members personally present where the number of members is not more than 1,000; fifteen where it is more than 1,000 but not more than 5,000; and thirty where it exceeds 5,000. For a private company, the statutory quorum is two members personally present. Check applicable company-specific exemptions or modifications and the articles before applying the default.

## Absence of quorum
If quorum is not present within half an hour after the appointed time, a meeting called by the Board is ordinarily adjourned to the same day in the next week at the same time and place, or to another date/time/place determined by the Board. A meeting called by requisitionists under section 100 stands cancelled. For an adjournment or change under section 103(2)(a), the company must give at least three days’ notice to members individually or by the specified newspaper advertisements.

If quorum is still absent within half an hour at the adjourned meeting, the members present form the quorum under section 103(3). Do not apply that final rule to a requisitionists’ meeting cancelled under section 103(2)(b).

## One Person Company limitation
Section 122(1) expressly provides that sections 98 and 100–111 do not apply to a One Person Company (OPC). Do not apply this section’s ordinary meeting mechanics to an OPC as if it were an ordinary company. Section 122(2)–(3) separately governs how ordinary business that would otherwise be transacted at an AGM is handled for an OPC. Confirm OPC status and apply the current section 122 procedure before advising.

sections.heading: Thresholds and articles
sections.body: For a public company, the default is five, fifteen or thirty members personally present depending on whether the membership count is up to 1,000, 1,001–5,000, or above 5,000. For a private company, the default is two personally present. Articles may require more.

sections.heading: Half-hour rule
sections.body: If quorum is absent within half an hour, a Board-called meeting is ordinarily adjourned under section 103(2)(a); a meeting called by requisitionists under section 100 is cancelled under section 103(2)(b).

sections.heading: Notice of adjournment or change
sections.body: For an adjournment or change under clause (a), give not less than three days’ notice to members individually or by the statutory newspaper-advertisement method.

sections.heading: Adjourned meeting
sections.body: If quorum is again absent within half an hour at the adjourned meeting, the members present constitute quorum under section 103(3). Keep this rule distinct from cancellation of a requisitionists’ meeting.

sections.heading: One Person Company limitation
sections.body: Section 122(1) disapplies sections 98 and 100–111 to an OPC. Section 122(2)–(3) supplies a separate procedure for ordinary business otherwise transacted at an AGM. Confirm whether the company is an OPC before applying this section.

examples.title: Quorum present
examples.body: A public company with 800 members has five members personally present and its articles do not require a larger quorum. On those assumptions, the statutory numerical threshold is met.

examples.title: Wrong threshold or no personal presence
examples.body: A public company with 2,000 members has only five members personally present, or a company counts proxies as personally present. The section’s numerical or personal-presence requirement may not be satisfied.

hypotheticals.question: A public company has 2,400 members. At the appointed time only ten members are personally present, and no larger quorum is specified in the articles. What follows if quorum remains absent after half an hour?
hypotheticals.analysis: The default threshold is fifteen members personally present for a public company with more than 1,000 and up to 5,000 members. If still absent after half an hour, identify whether the meeting was called by the Board or requisitionists: the former is ordinarily adjourned under section 103(2)(a), while the latter is cancelled under clause (b). Apply the notice requirement to an adjournment/change and the separate rule for the adjourned meeting.

caseLaw.point: The quorum for a public company is five members personally present where the member count is within the first band, and fifteen or thirty above that. A private company needs two. This is a statutory pointer, not a judgment.
